lines.text: What actually happens when I click a flashlight?
Light happens.
I could've said that.
Fine. Electricity only flows in a full loop. Out of the battery, and back in.
Batteries sit nose to tail. Plus end on minus end.
Like a tiny conga line.
Sure. A spring at the tail keeps them pressed tight together.
And a metal strip runs the length of the tube, back to the switch.
So what does my click do?
When it's off, there's a tiny gap. The loop is broken.
Click, and a metal piece bridges the gap. Loop closed. Light.
And why does it stay on?
A clicky tail has the same guts as a clicky pen. Click on. Click off.
So my flashlight is a pen with a sun in it.
Please never teach anyone anything.
Then why does mine flicker when I shake it?
Usually a little rust on the contacts. Rub them with a pencil eraser.
Or I just smack it.
Eraser. And now you know.
Hold on. Real talk...
